issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking an injunction is not unmaintainable merely because the plaint does not separately seek a declaration of title when the plaint, read as a whole, seeks to establish title as the basis for the injunction.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a perpetual injunction and expressly pleaded that the land had been transferred to their predecessor and that they were owners in possession.
The plaint relied on the asserted title as the basis for restraining interference, although it did not separately request a declaration of title.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the suit was not maintainable because it did not specifically seek a declaration of title was rejected. The plaint had to be read as a whole, and court fees had to be assessed accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: To determine the nature of a suit, the entire plaint must be read rather than only its relief portion. Where the plaint as a whole seeks to establish title as the basis for an injunction, the absence of a separately worded prayer for declaration does not make the suit unmaintainable. Court fees are to be assessed in accordance with the suit's nature. No earlier cases or specific provisions were cited.

predicates.injunction_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking an injunction against interference with possession.
predicates.plaint_asserts_title: The plaintiff pleaded title in the plaint as the basis for the requested injunction.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks an injunction and pleads title as its basis, the suit is not unmaintainable solely because it lacks a separate request for a declaration.

issues.legal_issue: The interpretation of revenue records that are not documents of title is not, by itself, a question of law in a second appeal.
material_facts: The first appellate court considered the revenue records and found that they did not support the plaintiffs' claim.
The High Court reversed that finding on the ground that the first appellate court had interpreted the records erroneously.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in treating its interpretation of the revenue records as a question of law, because the records were not documents of title.
issues.legal_principle: Revenue records are not documents of title, and the interpretation of a document that is not a document of title is not a question of law. No specific provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.second_appeal: The challenged decision was made while deciding a second appeal.
predicates.revenue_records_not_title_documents: The records relied on were revenue records and were not documents of title.
predicates.reversal_based_on_record_interpretation: The court reversed a factual finding because it considered the lower court's interpretation of those records erroneous.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, reversal based on interpretation of revenue records that are not documents of title does not turn that interpretation into a question of law.

issues.legal_issue: A second appeal must be reheard when the appellate court's approach is internally inconsistent and it reverses factual findings without valid reasons.
material_facts: The High Court made inconsistent observations about whether title was in issue in the suit.
It commented adversely on the first appellate court's findings about title and possession without giving valid reasons for doing so.
The first appellate court had separately considered title and possession and had found that the plaintiffs failed to prove possession at the alleged time of trespass.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's decision was set aside, and the second appeal was remitted for a fresh decision. Proper steps to assess and realise court fees on the plaint and appeal memoranda according to correct valuation were to be taken before rehearing.
issues.legal_principle: A second-appeal decision vitiated by an unsatisfactory approach, inconsistent treatment of the issues, or unjustified interference with factual findings cannot stand and may be set aside for a fresh decision. No specific provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.second_appeal: The challenged decision was made while deciding a second appeal.
predicates.inconsistent_issue_approach: The court treated whether a material issue was involved inconsistently in its decision.
predicates.factual_findings_reversed_without_valid_: The court reversed factual findings without giving valid reasons for doing so.

issues.definition: When a second-appeal decision takes an inconsistent approach to the issues and reverses factual findings without valid reasons, the decision is set aside and the appeal is remitted for a fresh decision.
